text: Norberto Santiago Raffo (27 April 1939 – 16 December 2008) was an Argentine footballer who played as a striker. He was the Copa Libertadores de América Topscorer in the 1967 season with 14 goals for Racing Club, the eventual champions, achieving the third highest goal total in a single Copa Libertadores season. Born in Avellaneda, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina, he played for both Avellaneda giants Independiente and Racing Club, winning major titles with both teams. He is best remembered by Banfield fans for scoring 68 goals in 180 games between 1960 and 1966, making him the third top scorer in the club's history. Raffo also played for Atlanta, Lanús, Altos Hornos Zapla in Argentina, Huachipato in Chile, and América de Cali in Colombia. He managed several Argentine clubs, most notably Lanús on multiple occasions and Banfield, as well as Argentino de Quilmes, El Porvenir, Gimnasia y Esgrima de Jujuy, Altos Hornos Zapla, and Talleres (RE). He had a long tenure in charge of the Lanús youth team from 1987 to 1996. His son, Néstor Santiago, is a former footballer for Racing Club.
